title: SCQA builder
prompt: Write two different SCQA formulations from the same context.
context: The Olympics has historically been one of the most unifying global events, drawing huge audiences and shared attention every two years. Recently, however, the Games have struggled to hold that same level of cultural relevance. The challenge is understanding why interest is fading and what could bring it back.

sampleAnswers.s: The Olympics remains one of the world's most recognizable sports properties, with unmatched history, global reach, athlete prestige, and symbolic power.
sampleAnswers.c: But recognition is no longer converting into cultural relevance. Audiences now encounter the Games through fragmented feeds, isolated clips, louder political and commercial signals, and fewer shared rituals, so the Olympics risks feeling less like a rare global moment and more like another stream of optional content.
sampleAnswers.q: How can LA 2028 convert the Olympics' unmatched recognition into renewed cultural relevance without chasing trends, weakening neutrality, or diluting the brand?
sampleAnswers.a: LA 2028 should rebuild Olympic relevance by treating the Games as a coherent cultural ritual, not just a content property: design shared appointment moments, build athlete-led story arcs that make stakes accumulate over time, and enforce a disciplined editorial and partner system that protects prestige, neutrality, and meaning across every channel.

sampleAnswers.q: Rather than trying to win back every audience at once, which single audience should LA 2028 prioritize to rebuild the Olympics' cultural relevance fastest?
sampleAnswers.a: LA 2028 should prioritize younger, casual sports fans over legacy loyalists: this group is the most reachable through short-form and creator-led content, the most likely to turn single moments into recurring attention, and the audience whose renewed engagement would most convincingly signal that the Games still matter culturally.
